songs.name: Sitting On Top Of The World
And We Bid You Good Night

supporting_acts: New Riders of the Purple Sage

ai_show_review.summary: Stunning acoustic/electric blend; epic “To Lay Me Down” and tight jams
ai_show_review.blurb: The show delivers an immaculate acoustic set that flows into a high‑energy electric second half. Standout moments include the mournful “To Lay Me Down,” the soaring “Not Fade Away > Caution > Feedback” sequence, and a fiery “Easy Wind.” Jerry’s lead work and Phil’s warm bass anchor a performance that ranks among the Fillmore classics.
ai_show_review.review:
September 20, 1970 at the Fillmore East captures the Dead at a creative peak. The first set unfurls an acoustic tapestry—“Uncle John’s Band,” “Ripple,” “To Lay Me Down,” and “Truckin’” among others—enhanced by guest mandolin from David Nelson and fiddle‑like textures from David Grisman, while Pigpen’s organ adds a soulful undercurrent. Jerry Garcia’s guitar on “To Lay Me Down” is described as solemn and longing, perfectly complementing the mournful piano that threads through the set. Phil Lesh provides a warm, woody bass foundation that grounds both acoustic numbers and the ensuing electric surge.

The second set explodes with kinetic power: “Not Fade Away” rockets into an unbridled “Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) > Feedback” jam that many reviewers call “monster,” followed by the breezy “Easy Wind” and a jubilant “Sugar Magnolia.” Bob Weir shines on “Easy Wind,” trading searing leads with Jerry, while his vocal grit lifts the acoustic “Truckin’.” The dual drumming of Mickey Hart and Bill Kreutzmann drives the improvisations forward, even if the drum mix occasionally peaks. Across all recordings the performance is consistently praised as “locked in” and “legendary,” despite some tape hiss on older sources. The standout soundboard capture (gd1970-09-20.140664.sbd.boswell…) offers crystal‑clear audio that lets every nuance of this landmark show shine.

rating_calculation.sentiment_rationale: The majority of recordings (5 out of 9) are marked positive, highlighting exceptional playing, seamless set flow, and guest contributions. No consistent negative remarks appear; mixed‑sentiment sources still praise key moments. This strong, uniform enthusiasm warrants a high positive adjustment.

best_recording.reason: Excellent soundboard source with crystal‑clear mix, no dropouts, and the most praised capture of the iconic “To Lay Me Down” performance.

key_highlights: Epic, mournful rendition of “To Lay Me Down” featuring Garcia’s soaring lead and piano accompaniment
"Not Fade Away > Caution (Do Not Stop On Tracks) > Feedback" jam that erupts into a monster improvisation
Acoustic gems like “Easy Wind,” “Truckin’” and the mandolin‑enhanced set
Guest appearances by David Nelson and David Grisman add unique texture

band_performance.Jerry: Delivers a solemn, longing lead on “To Lay Me Down” and rides the high‑energy jams with an almost ‘out of control’ intensity, especially during the second‑set improvisations.
band_performance.Phil: Provides a warm, woody bass tone that grounds both acoustic numbers and the electric surge; his electric bass addition on the acoustic set is highlighted as a unique moment.
band_performance.Bob: Shines on “Easy Wind” with searing lead work and vocal grit, and his rhythm/lead duel with Jerry adds excitement to the electric side; praised for vocal delivery on acoustic “Truckin’.”
band_performance.Pigpen: Organ and piano textures enrich the acoustic set; mournful piano on “To Lay Me Down” is singled out as a special contribution.
band_performance.Mickey: Drums are energetic and drive the jams forward, though some mixes push the drum level high in spots.
band_performance.Billy: Provides solid, propulsive drumming alongside Mickey, helping maintain the show’s relentless momentum.
